explanations: luna: The source section glosses خاشع as including a raki, one who bows; this command explicitly joins prayer to وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ, bowing with the worshippers. | terra: The command to establish prayer and bow with those who bow gives the Quranic act behind the section's dictionary statement that the humble one is also the one in rukūʿ.

luna: This verse joins prayer with الخَاشِعِينَ and says it is burdensome except for them; it sharpens the source section’s pairing of prayer-posture and weary labor by giving humility a different relation to prayer. | terra: Prayer is described as heavy except for الْخَاشِعِينَ, explicitly joining صلاة to the section's خشع root and showing inward humility making the bodily act possible.
terra: The خَاشِعِينَ of 2:45 are those who expect to meet their Lord and return to Him, grounding voluntary humility in awareness of the very encounter where false refusal ends.
luna: The source section names prayer as comprising bowing and prostration; this verse names both postures, الرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ, in the purified House.

luna: The source section reads نَاصِبَة through upright, tiring posture; here the maintained prayers are paired with وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ, standing devoutly before God. | terra: Guarding the prayers is paired with standing devoutly before Allah, giving the voluntary upright worship that the section hears inside نَاصِبَةٌ.
terra: Angels call Zechariah while he stands praying in the sanctuary, explicitly uniting upright posture with صلاة.

luna: The source section connects a bowed face with the raki and prayer’s bodily acts; Mary is told to prostrate and bow, وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي, as worship. | terra: Mary is commanded to be devout, prostrate, and bow with those who bow, gathering the voluntary worship postures sounded by the section.

terra: Everything in the heavens and earth submits to Allah willingly or unwillingly and returns to Him, expressing both the choice now and the unavoidable return behind the section's two kinds of bending.
terra: On the Day when faces darken, those faces are addressed for disbelief and told to taste punishment; the face reveals the inward refusal before punishment follows.
luna: The source section’s weary upright posture and prayer’s prostration meet in this community that stands reciting by night and is وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ, a willing devotional scene.

luna: These believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, then pray to be protected from the Fire; the ayah joins bodily states, remembrance, supplication, and fire in one scene. | terra: Believers remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying down, showing ذكر inhabiting every bodily orientation rather than depending on one posture.
luna: Some People of the Book are described as خَاشِعِينَ لله while believing in revelation; the source section’s root for a bowed face thus also marks voluntary humility before God.
luna: The source section’s root ص ل ي links entering fire with ritual prayer; this ayah uses that same root for the blaze awaiting those who consume orphans’ property.
luna: This ayah says those who commit aggression will be made to enter a fire, using the source section’s root ص ل ي in its fire-entry sense.
luna: The rejected signs lead to a fire that repeatedly burns and replaces their skins; the fire-entry verb belongs to the source section’s ص ل ي root.

luna: The battle prayer is arranged around one group prostrating while the other keeps watch, then the second group praying; it gives a concrete scene of prayer’s bodily sujud under strain. | terra: During the danger prayer, one group's completed prostration marks its turn in the صلاة, a Quranic instance of prayer concretely constituted by bodily sujūd.

luna: After prayer, believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides; this ayah itself continues prayer into dhikr through bodily states, the relation the source section’s lexical note raises. | terra: After prayer, Allah is to be remembered standing, sitting, and lying, then prayer re-established; remembrance and bodily positions are held together rather than reduced to posture.
luna: The source section links turning away with fire and failed worship; this ayah pairs turning away from the Messenger with being made to enter Hell, using the same fire-entry root ص ل ي.
terra: Hypocrites stand for prayer lazily, showing off, and remember Allah only a little; the ayah exposes how an upright prayer posture can remain spiritually empty.
terra: Those who establish prayer are described while bowing, making the prayer-rukūʿ relation explicit in a single ayah.
terra: Iblis refuses the command to prostrate and grounds the refusal in superiority, making pride the motive for rejecting voluntary lowering.
terra: After refusing prostration, Iblis is ordered down because arrogance is forbidden there and is cast among the debased, turning self-exaltation into compulsory lowliness.
terra: The same refusal passage ends with Hell being filled by Iblis and his followers, supplying the fiery outcome beyond the forced descent in 7:13.

luna: This commands calling on God humbly and privately; it concretely connects the source section’s dictionary sense of dhikr as supplication with voluntary humility rather than judgment-day disgrace.
terra: The command to remember the Lord inwardly with humility and fear makes ذكر a quiet voluntary lowering of the self before the prostration of 7:206.
terra: Those near the Lord are not arrogant about worshipping Him; they glorify Him and prostrate, opposing pride with willing bodily submission.

luna: This verse brings remembrance and prayer into one account of believers: God’s mention moves their hearts, and they يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ; it clarifies the source section’s prayer/remembrance link.

terra: Their so-called prayer at the House is only whistling and clapping, and the ayah immediately orders them to taste punishment; it marks the boundary between the posture or label of صلاة and true worship.
terra: At death the angels strike the disbelievers' faces and backs and make them taste burning punishment, linking the death-setting around 75:31-32 to the section's face-and-fire scene.
terra: Their offerings are rejected because they come to prayer only lazily and spend unwillingly, another boundary between performing صلاة bodily and submitting willingly.

luna: This description of repentant worshippers names them as bowing and prostrating, the ritual bodily acts the source section hears beside its words for bowed faces and burning. | terra: Bowing and prostrating appear among the defining qualities of faithful worshippers, making those postures signs of a whole obedient life.
terra: No thirst, fatigue نَصَبٌ, or hunger borne in Allah's path goes unwritten as a righteous deed; this is purposeful, credited weariness against the exhausted body ending in fire.
terra: The Prophet is asked whether he would compel people to believe when Allah could have made all believe, defining the no-compulsion side of the section's reminder and later forced abasement.

terra: The command to establish prayer is followed by the assurance that good deeds remove evils and that this is a reminder for those who remember, joining صلاة and ذكر with an effective moral result.

luna: This says all in heaven and earth prostrate to God willingly or unwillingly; its explicit willing/compelled boundary sharpens the source section’s contrast between worldly invitation and judgment-day inability. | terra: All in the heavens and earth prostrate willingly or unwillingly, expressly stating the voluntary/compelled boundary that the section finds between worship now and abasement then.
luna: Those who exchange gratitude for disbelief settle their people in ruin, Hell, where they burn; the fire-entry verb is the source section’s root ص ل ي.
terra: Fire covering their faces supplies a compact parallel to the sequence from faces in 88:2 to burning in 88:4.
terra: Paradise is a place where no نَصَبٌ touches its people, the direct reversal of the weary condition named by نَاصِبَةٌ in 88:3.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord's praise and be among those who prostrate, coupling spoken praise with voluntary bodily lowering.
terra: The command to worship until certainty arrives makes the prostration of 15:98 a lifelong stance maintained up to death.
terra: Created things cast inclining shadows that prostrate to Allah while abased, turning visible downward inclination into a sign of universal submission.
terra: Every creature and the angels prostrate to Allah without arrogance, extending the inclining shadows of 16:48 into conscious willing submission.
terra: They fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded, supplying the obedient inward stance behind the prostration of 16:49.
terra: If they turn away, the Messenger's duty is only clear conveyance, another precise limit on the reminder's authority before judgment.
terra: The Last-Day gathering on faces, followed in the same ayah by Hell as abode, directly combines bodily abasement and fire.
luna: When the Qur’an is recited, people given knowledge fall in prostration; this is the voluntary response whose judgment-day counterpart the source section finds in 68:43.

luna: The source section’s root خ ش ع includes devotional bowing; here listeners fall on their faces weeping and خُشُوعًا increases, a chosen response unlike the later humiliation. | terra: They fall on their faces weeping and the revelation increases their خُشُوعًا, showing a face lowered voluntarily through receptive remembrance rather than humiliation.
terra: The travellers say that their journey has brought them نَصَبًا, giving the ordinary bodily fatigue from which the section's description of نَاصِبَةٌ draws.
terra: The question about the greatest losers in deeds plausibly opens a reading of 88:3 as futile exertion, though the section itself develops bodily weariness more explicitly than lost works.
terra: Their striving is lost in worldly life while they think they are doing well, a concrete parallel for exertion whose outward labor does not yield salvation.
terra: Their deeds come to nothing because they denied the signs and the meeting with their Lord, explaining the failed destination of the lost striving in 18:104.

luna: When the Merciful’s signs are recited, these servants fall سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا; their chosen prostration and tears contrast with the forced call and humiliation in 68:43. | terra: When the Merciful's signs are recited, the prophets fall prostrate and weep; this receptive posture is the immediate opposite of the successors who neglect prayer in 19:59.

luna: This generation أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ and followed desires; the loss of prayer gives a specific negative counterpart to the source section’s link between prayer and the burned. | terra: Successors who neglected prayer and followed desires will meet ruin, directly connecting abandoned صلاة with a punitive end.
luna: This ayah identifies who is most deserving of burning in Hell, using the same ص ل ي root that the source section hears in 88:4.

luna: The source section says the root ذ ك ر includes prayer; this command joins إقامة الصلاة to لِذِكْرِي, prayer explicitly performed for God’s remembrance. | terra: أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي directly joins prayer to remembrance, supporting the section's dictionary sense of ذكر as prayer while preserving both ideas.
terra: The revealed rule that punishment falls on whoever denies and turns away closely restates the movement from 88:23 to 88:24.

luna: At the Resurrection the voices خَشَعَتْ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ; the source section applies khushu to faces and prayer, while this ayah transfers that abasement to sound. | terra: On that Day even voices خَشَعَتْ before the Merciful until only a whisper is heard, extending the section's forced visible humility from faces to speech.

luna: On the Day of Resurrection, faces are humbled before the Living and wrongdoing is disappointed; this is a judgment-day face posture distinct from the source section’s bowed face, but concretely echoes its scene.
terra: Whoever turns away from Allah's remembrance receives a constricted life and is raised blind, making refusal of ذكر become compelled deprivation at resurrection.
terra: The command to enjoin prayer on one's family and persevere in it presents صلاة as sustained exertion whose provision and outcome remain with Allah.
terra: The disbelievers cannot keep the Fire from their faces or backs, showing the total bodily helplessness implicit in the section's compelled posture.

luna: The section’s account of dhikr includes supplication, and it names خاشع; here servants call on God and are described as خَاشِعِينَ, voluntary humility before the day’s humiliation. | terra: Zechariah's household call on Allah in hope and fear and are خَاشِعِينَ toward Him, a devotional use of the section's root outside formal prayer posture.
terra: Creation prostrates to Allah, while the same ayah distinguishes many people for whom punishment is due; it puts submission and punishment on the exact boundary the section explores.
terra: The sanctuary is purified for those circling, standing, bowing, and prostrating, gathering all the worship postures sounded by the section into one sacred scene.
luna: When God is mentioned, hearts tremble; the same ayah names patience through affliction and maintaining prayer, connecting remembrance and bodily endurance to worship.

luna: This command to bow and prostrate, ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا, gives the bodily prayer postures that the source section hears behind its words for bowed faces and burning. | terra: The command to bow, prostrate, and worship the Lord lays out the voluntary bodily sequence that the section hears beside bending and burning.

luna: The source section says خاشع also names the one who bows in prayer; this describes believers as خَاشِعُونَ in their prayer, a voluntary devotional posture set against the humbled faces of 88:2. | terra: The section explicitly hears prayer inside خَاشِعَةٌ; here the successful believers are خَاشِعُونَ precisely in their prayer, the saving worldly counterpart to the humbled faces of 88:2.

luna: Here the fire burns their faces, تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ, joining the source section’s separate face and fire images in one punishment scene. | terra: The Fire scorches their faces and leaves them grimacing, presenting the face itself as the site where burning becomes visible.
terra: These people let no trade distract them from remembrance and prayer because they fear a Day when hearts and eyes overturn; chosen remembrance and صلاة answer the future upheaval of the face.

luna: People are gathered عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ; the face directed toward punishment links the bowed face with the fire-bound body in the source section. | terra: Gathering people on their faces toward Hell makes the face's downward posture part of their compulsory journey to fire.

luna: The source section contrasts a worldly invitation to prostrate with the later humiliating call; here people refuse the worldly command اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ, clarifying the voluntary side of that boundary. | terra: When commanded to prostrate to the Merciful, they question the command and recoil; their refusal sharply contrasts with the willing nighttime prostration in 25:64.

luna: The source section links an upright, tiring body to ritual prayer; these servants spend the night سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا before their Lord, joining prostration and standing as willing worship. | terra: The servants of the Merciful spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord, combining the two voluntary postures whose sounds the section detects.
terra: Immediately after their prostration and standing, they ask that Hell's punishment be turned away, explicitly placing worship posture against burning punishment.
terra: Allah could send a sign that would leave their necks permanently bowed to it; this hypothetical forced submission clarifies why the prophetic reminder leaves room for a voluntary response.
terra: The deviators are toppled headlong into Hell, another concrete loss of bodily control at entry into punishment.
terra: Allah sees the Prophet when he rises or stands; the following movement among those prostrating makes worshipful standing a likely, though context-dependent, contribution here.
terra: The Prophet's movement among those prostrating places his bodily action within a worshipping community, completing the standing scene of 26:218.
terra: Faces are cast down into the Fire and the sufferers are told they receive what they did, making bodily inversion the disclosed outcome of action.

luna: The source section says dhikr may mean prayer; this verse commands prayer and then says وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ, placing the two acts in an explicit relation. | terra: Prayer restrains indecency and Allah's remembrance is greater, another explicit meeting of صلاة and ذكر that explains why the section can hear remembrance within prayer.
terra: Luqman commands his son to establish prayer and patiently bear what befalls him, joining صلاة to purposeful endurance rather than futile exhaustion.

luna: When reminded of God’s signs, believers fall in prostration, glorify Him, and are not arrogant; this joins reminder to voluntary sujud, against the later forced call. | terra: Those who truly believe respond to being reminded of the signs by falling in prostration without arrogance, the voluntary response sought by the reminder in 88:21.
terra: The wrongdoer is reminded of his Lord's signs and then turns away from them; this condenses the movement from the command to remind in 88:21 to turning away in 88:23.

luna: This verse places الخَاشِعِينَ and those who remember God often, الذَّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا, among the same believing qualities, meeting two roots the source section names. | terra: The humble men and women and those who remember Allah much share one promise of forgiveness and reward, joining the section's خشع and ذكر motifs on the saving side.
terra: Faces are turned about in the Fire while their owners wish they had obeyed Allah and the Messenger, joining the punished face to regret over refused obedience.
terra: The inhabitants of the lasting home praise Allah because neither نَصَبٌ nor weariness touches them, setting enduring relief against the section's exhausted condemned body.
luna: The condemned are told to enter the Fire that day for their disbelief; the command uses the source section’s ص ل ي fire-entry root.
luna: The ayah excludes from misguidance those destined to burn in Hell, using the source section’s ص ل ي root for entering the fire.
luna: David falls bowing and turns back after recognizing his trial; the source section says a bowed face also evokes the raki, making this chosen bowing a counterpart to humiliation.
terra: Job names نُصْبٍ and torment as an affliction that has touched him, showing exhausted suffering in worldly trial rather than as the fixed Last-Day condition.
luna: In the exchange between Hell’s groups, this ayah says the new arrivals will burn in the Fire, using the source section’s ص ل ي root.

luna: This asks whether one who spends the night prostrating and standing, سَاجِدًا وَقَائِمًا, fearing the Hereafter, is like one who does not; it links the source section’s prayer-postures to the judgment that separates faces. | terra: The night worshipper alternates prostration and standing while fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy; purposeful qiyām and sujūd oppose the exhausted body carried unknowingly into fire.
terra: Woe belongs to hearts hardened against Allah's remembrance, the exact inward reversal of a heart humbling voluntarily to reminder.

luna: The revealed word makes skins shiver, then soften at God’s remembrance; this gives a bodily response to dhikr alongside the source section’s connection between bodily submission and remembrance. | terra: Revelation makes skins shiver and then skins and hearts soften toward Allah's remembrance, a specific bodily response to ذكر that stops short of forced abasement.

luna: This asks about one who shields his face from the worst punishment on Judgment Day; it makes the face itself the site of exposure to the consequence paired with 88:2, 88:3, and 88:4. | terra: The person forced to shield the evil punishment with his face embodies the loss of bodily freedom that distinguishes Last-Day abasement from chosen prostration.
terra: On the Day of resurrection liars against Allah have blackened faces, and the ayah locates the arrogant in Hell; face, pride, and punishment converge.

luna: God invites people to call on Him, while those too proud to worship will enter Hell humbled; this directly joins supplication, refusal of worship, punishment, and humiliation. | terra: Those too proud for Allah's worship will enter Hell abased, directly turning refused voluntary worship into compulsory humiliation and fire.
terra: Shackles around necks and chains by which people are dragged portray the condemned body placed under compulsory restraint before the burning in 40:72.
terra: They are dragged into boiling water and then burned in the Fire, completing the forced bodily movement begun in 40:71.
terra: The command forbids prostration to sun or moon and directs it to their Creator, marking correct worship by both bodily act and rightful object.
terra: The earth is seen خَاشِعَةً and then stirred to life by water, a secondary use in which low stillness is receptive and revivable rather than punitive humiliation.

luna: The source section’s root خ ش ع describes the bowed face; these wrongdoers are خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ as they are exposed to the Fire, an explicit judgment-day humiliation. | terra: The condemned are shown to the Fire خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ and looking furtively; humiliation, lowered sight, and exposure to fire converge as they do across 88:2-4.
terra: If they turn away, the Prophet is told he was not sent as their guardian and owes only conveyance, closely matching reminder without control in 88:21-23.

luna: The source section joins face and prayer posture; this verse makes prostration visible on believers’ faces, سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ, as a mark of worship. | terra: رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا and the mark of prostration on their faces unite voluntary bowing, prostration, and the face, reversing the section's compelled mark of humiliation.
terra: The Prophet is told he is not a compeller over them and must remind by the Quran whoever fears the warning, an especially close parallel to the reminder-without-control stance of 88:21-22.
terra: The command to remind because reminder benefits believers identifies the receptive audience for the same prophetic act commanded in 88:21.
luna: The disbelievers are thrust toward the Fire of Hell; this forced movement toward burning contrasts with the call to prostrate in 68:43 and extends the source section’s judgment scene.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn from whoever turns from Allah's remembrance and wants only worldly life, identifying the present refusal behind later humiliation.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for, setting accountable, owned effort against an image of exhausted labor whose value is in question.
terra: Each person's striving will be seen, so bodily exertion cannot conceal its direction or purpose at judgment.
terra: Striving will then be fully repaid, completing the reversal in which meaningful effort receives its exact outcome rather than merely ending in fatigue.

luna: At the close of a warning, the audience is commanded to prostrate and worship; it is a direct voluntary call that contrasts with the later inability in 68:43. | terra: The direct command to prostrate to Allah and worship states the willing bodily response whose refusal later becomes compulsory abasement.

luna: The dead come from graves with خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ; the same root and lowered gaze place the section’s bowed-face image in another Resurrection scene. | terra: خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ places humbled eyes on people emerging from the graves, fixing the section's bodily inclination within resurrection rather than voluntary worship.

luna: Those punished are يَسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ; the face carried into fire joins the source section’s bowed faces and burning as a stark forced posture. | terra: Being dragged on their faces into the Fire literalizes the section's bond between an abased body and burning.
luna: The fate of the people of the left includes burning in Hell; the word for that burning belongs to the ص ل ي root that the source section also links to prayer.

luna: The source section brings bowed humility and remembrance together; this ayah asks believers’ hearts to تَخْشَعَ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ, directly joining the root خ ش ع to dhikr. | terra: The call for believers' hearts to تَخْشَعَ at Allah's remembrance makes humility a voluntary present response to reminder, before it becomes an imposed outward condition.

luna: The source section’s root خ ش ع describes a bowed face and worshipper; here a mountain would be خَاشِعًا before God’s revelation and split from fear, showing the same root applied beyond the human prayer-body. | terra: A mountain would be seen خَاشِعًا and split from fear if the Quran descended upon it; the imagined humbled object exposes the hardness of a hearer who resists reminder.

luna: When Friday prayer is called, people are told فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ; this joins prayer and remembrance, as in the source section’s secondary sense of dhikr. | terra: When the call to Friday prayer is made, believers are commanded to hasten to ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ, a Quranic setting in which remembrance names the act of communal prayer.
terra: After the prayer ends, believers disperse and continue remembering Allah much, showing both the prayer sense of ذكر in 62:9 and remembrance extending beyond the rite.
terra: Walking fallen on one's face is contrasted with walking upright on a straight path, making downward and upright posture disclose two contrary orientations before their final outcomes.
terra: When the promised event draws near, the disbelievers' faces become distressed and they are told this is what they demanded, making the face disclose belated recognition.

luna: This ayah itself stages the judgment-day call to prostrate and inability to do so; 68:43, the source section’s cited neighbor, adds the lowered eyes and the memory of being sound. | terra: The summons to prostrate when they can no longer do so supplies the immediate Last-Day action completed by the humbled eyes and remembered earlier summons in 68:43.

luna: The source section’s root خ ش ع names the lowered face and a worshipper’s bow; here خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ is joined to the call to prostrate while they had been سالمون, making voluntary worship and judgment-day humiliation meet. | terra: The humbled eyes, engulfing humiliation, and recalled call to prostrate while sound make this the section's exact boundary between voluntary worldly bowing and compelled abasement on that Day.
luna: The command to burn the condemned in Hell uses the same ص ل ي root as the source section’s fire-entry word.

luna: The passage names the blazing fire Laza, another direct fire scene for the source section’s image of entering a hot fire. | terra: This ayah identifies the threatened destination as a blazing Fire, beginning a passage that names turning away and then exempts those devoted to prayer.
luna: This ayah describes the flame stripping the scalp; 70:15 names Laza, while this ayah adds the burning body’s injury to the source section’s fire image.

luna: The preceding ayat establish Laza as a destructive flame; this ayah says it calls whoever turned away, joining the fire to the same turning-away stance named in the source section. | terra: The blaze calls the person who turned his back and turned away, supplying the refusal that connects its fire in 70:15 with the prayerful exception in 70:22.
terra: The worshippers are expressly excepted from the preceding fiery outcome, another direct Quranic junction between صلاة and burning.
terra: Constancy in prayer defines the worshippers excepted from the blaze, showing sustained willing devotion rather than a momentary bodily pose.
terra: Guarding their prayer repeats the passage's decisive attribute before their honored destination is named, making care for صلاة the counterpart to turning away.
terra: Those who guard prayer are honored in gardens, completing the outcome opposite both the blaze earlier in the passage and the humbled eyes in 70:44.

luna: The resurrected rush as if toward a نُصُبٍ, an erected object; the source section’s root ن ص ب names upright standing until fatigue, while 70:44 adds the lowered eyes and humiliation. | terra: They rush from the graves as if toward a نُصُب; this different noun of the section's نصب root stands immediately before their humbled eyes in 70:44, placing an erected goal beside lowered bodies.

luna: On the day they emerge from graves, their eyes are خَاشِعَةٌ and humiliation covers them; the same rooted lowering on judgment day extends the source section’s bowed face. | terra: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ and humiliation covering them on the promised Day closely restage the section's humbled faces as involuntary exposure.
terra: Allah's servant stands calling upon Him while a crowd presses around; this may preserve worshipful qiyām, though the ayah itself says invocation rather than explicitly naming formal prayer.

luna: The night command explicitly requires standing for prayer except for a little; 73:20 later explains the long vigil’s burden and relief, giving context for the source section’s weary upright stance. | terra: The command قُمِ اللَّيْلَ makes prolonged standing a chosen night devotion, the Quranic qiyām heard alongside the section's definition of upright exertion.
terra: Remembering the Lord's name and devoting oneself wholly follows the night-standing command, paralleling the remembrance-and-prayer sequence in 87:15.

luna: The Prophet and believers are described standing long portions of the night, then given relief and told to recite what is easy and establish prayer; this makes the source section’s tiring upright stance concrete. | terra: Allah acknowledges the Prophet and a group standing through large portions of the night and then grants a practicable measure, distinguishing measured devotion from endless exhaustion.
terra: The resistant hearer turns his back and grows arrogant, a bodily and inward refusal that leads directly toward Saqar in 74:26.

luna: The threat to burn a denier in Saqar uses the exact ص ل ي root that the source section also hears in prayer. | terra: The threat to burn him in Saqar uses the section's fire-entering branch of صلى and supplies the outcome of the arrogance and turning in 74:23.

luna: The question أَيُّ شَيْءٍ سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ names the fire that 74:43 answers by naming the absence of prayer; its contribution is to frame prayer as an answer about entry into Saqar. | terra: The question مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ names the fire whose first answer is failure to pray in 74:43, recreating the section's prayer/fire junction across adjacent ayat.

luna: The source section links the root ص ل ي in entering fire with ritual prayer; this answer says لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ, and 74:42 supplies the question that places the answer in Saqar. | terra: Their answer, that they were not among those who prayed, places omitted صلاة as the first stated reason for reaching Saqar in 74:42.
terra: The question asks why they turn away from التَّذْكِرَةِ, directly coupling reminder with the very motion of refusal developed beside 88:21-23.
terra: Radiant faces on that Day provide a direct reversal of the humbled condemned faces in the section.
terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, showing chosen faith culminating in an uplifted gaze rather than the lowered gaze of humiliation.
terra: Other faces on that Day are gloomy, a close facial counterpart to the section's humbled faces within the same surah that names failure to pray.
terra: Those gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity, making their posture and expression the bodily anticipation of punishment.
terra: The soul reaching the collarbones locates the later statement that he neither affirmed nor prayed at the closing threshold when voluntary action is ending.
terra: The drive that day is to the Lord, so the subsequent denial, turning away, and failure to pray are framed by a return the denier cannot resist.

luna: The source section directly cites فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ; the negated prayer is the same ص ل ي word-family whose other branch in 88:4 means entering fire. | terra: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّى names failure to affirm and pray at life's closing passage, supplying the refused voluntary prayer behind the later compelled posture.

luna: The source section directly cites كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ and connects turning away to 88:23; this ayah’s denial and turning away specify the stance paired with failure to pray in 75:31. | terra: وَلَكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى makes denial and turning away the sequel to not praying in 75:31, directly clarifying the turner-away of 88:23.
terra: The command to remember the Lord's name morning and evening begins a compact sequence in which remembrance leads into nighttime prostration.
terra: Prostration during the night and long glorification give the bodily worship that completes the remembrance command of 76:25.
terra: When they are told ارْكَعُوا they do not bow; this refused worldly rukūʿ is the sharp reversal behind the inevitable lowered posture on the Last Day.

luna: The scene gives humiliated eyes, أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ, using the source section’s root for a face lowered at the Resurrection. | terra: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives the same humbled gaze amid the resurrection shock, another direct staging of the section's compulsory bodily humility.
terra: Faces on that Day have dust upon them, beginning another judgment portrait in which the condemned condition is visibly borne by the face.
terra: Darkness covers those dusty faces, adding an engulfing visible abasement before their owners are identified in 80:42.
terra: The dusty, darkened faces belong to disbelieving transgressors, tying the Last-Day facial state to their prior refusal.
terra: Humanity will stand before the Lord of the worlds on the Day of resurrection, making standing then an imposed summons rather than chosen qiyām in worship.
luna: After being veiled from their Lord, these deniers are said to burn in Hell; this is another direct use of the source section’s ص ل ي fire-entry root.
terra: Every human is laboring strenuously toward the Lord and will meet Him; this gives the unavoidable destination of work and weariness without assuming that every exertion is worship.
luna: The condemned will burn in a blazing fire; the ayah uses the source section’s ص ل ي root in the same fire-entry sense.

luna: When the Qur’an is recited, these people do not prostrate; their refusal is a specific worldly counterpart to the later call to sujud described in 68:43. | terra: When the Quran is recited to them they do not prostrate, another direct refusal of voluntary sujūd before the Day when bodily abasement cannot be refused.
terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَى gives the parallel command to remind that opens the same nearby sequence ending in fire or prayer.
terra: The one who fears will remember, supplying the receptive hearer of the reminder before 87:15 joins remembering the Lord's name to prayer.
terra: The most wretched avoids the reminder and then enters the greater Fire, tracing the refusal that lies between reminder and burning.

luna: The source section explicitly pairs its root ص ل ي senses: this ayah says يَصْلَى النار الكبرى, the fire-entry sense, beside 87:15’s prayer sense. | terra: يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرَى gives the same fire-entering branch heard in 88:4; its proximity to prayer in 87:15 makes the section's two senses audible together.
terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies himself, introducing the person who remembers and prays in 87:15 as the saving counterpart to the burner in 87:12.

luna: The source section explicitly pairs this root’s senses: here one remembers his Lord and then فَصَلَّىٰ, the prayer sense, set against the fire-entry in 87:12. | terra: ذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى joins remembrance to the prayer branch of the section's صلى root, opposite the person who يَصْلَى the greater fire in 87:12.

luna: The source section’s fire-entry root ص ل ي recurs in لَا يَصْلَاهَا; this passage makes burning a boundary, with 92:16 identifying the denier who turns away. | terra: لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى uses the fire-entering sense of صلى and is immediately defined by denial and turning away in 92:16.

luna: The source section links 88:23’s turning away and disbelief with 75:32; this ayah repeats كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, while 92:15 supplies its own passage’s fire consequence. | terra: الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى identifies the one who burns as the one who denied and turned away, almost exactly unpacking the movement from 88:23 to punishment.
luna: After 92:15 and 92:16 describe who burns and why, this ayah’s own contribution is that the most God-conscious will be kept away from that same fire, a boundary in the section’s burning image.

luna: The source section’s root ن ص ب is glossed as standing until weariness and this verse is cited directly: فَانصَبْ commands the addressed Prophet to exert himself once free. | terra: The command فَانصَبْ uses the section's نصب root for rising to strenuous devotion, turning upright weariness into a commanded act rather than the condemned body's exhaustion in 88:3.
luna: The preceding 94:7 commands exertion; this ayah directs the longing toward the Lord, completing the devotional orientation of the standing-and-effort command quoted by the source section.
terra: The passage singles out one who forbids, setting human resistance against the servant's prayer in 96:10 and the final command to prostrate.
terra: عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّى identifies the forbidden act as a servant's prayer, placing chosen صلاة under opposition rather than abandonment.

luna: The imperative وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ makes prostration a willing approach to God, the devotional counterpart to the compelled prostration described in 68:43. | terra: The servant is told not to obey the opponent but to prostrate and draw near, making voluntary downward movement the route to nearness.
luna: The concluding image is a حَامِيَة fire, the same distinctive hot-fire description as 88:4, now attached to the fate of one whose scale is light.
terra: Woe is pronounced over people still called الْمُصَلِّينَ, warning that the prayer-name and posture alone do not prevent the condemned outcome.
terra: Those worshippers are heedless of their own prayer, specifying the inward failure that lets prayer-shaped action remain empty.
terra: Their display for other people completes the boundary: visible worship posture can be directed toward an audience rather than toward God.
luna: Abu Lahab is promised burning in a flaming fire, another direct instance of the source section’s ص ل ي fire-entry root.
